concepts.label: Running SQL++ Queries from the Java SDK
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the page's subject is the client API surface for issuing an arbitrary SQL++ query (Cluster.query()/Scope.query(), QueryOptions, QueryResult, reactive/async variants), not any single named statement. No specific DDL/DML statement (CREATE INDEX, GRANT, etc.) is the subject here - the example query is a plain SELECT. See cross_product_finding.

relations.subject: sdk:sqlpp-queries-with-sdk
relations.evidence: A query is always performed at the `Cluster` level, using the `query` method. It takes the statement as a required argument and then allows to provide additional options if needed.

relations.subject: sdk:sqlpp-queries-with-sdk
relations.evidence: In addition to the blocking API on `Cluster`, the SDK provides reactive and async APIs on `ReactiveCluster` or `AsyncCluster` respectively.

relations.subject: sdk:sqlpp-queries-with-sdk
relations.evidence: It is possible to query off the [Scope level] ... _with Couchbase Server release 7.x_, using the `scope.query()` method.

relations.subject: sdk:sqlpp-queries-with-sdk
relations.evidence: If you are using a cluster older than Couchbase Server 6.5, it is required that there is at least one bucket open before performing a cluster-level query. If you fail to do so, the SDK will return a `FeatureNotAvailableException`.

cross_product_finding: This page is the clearest 'client API, not a statement' case in the batch: the query it demonstrates is a plain ad-hoc SELECT, and the entire page is organized around the SDK's own vocabulary (QueryOptions, QueryResult, QueryMetaData, ReactiveCluster/AsyncCluster) rather than around any named SQL++ statement. It never names CREATE INDEX, GRANT, or any other DDL statement that has an established n1ql:* concept id in the registry - it only gestures at index-building in passing ('Note that building indexes is covered in some detail on the Query concept page') without describing a specific statement. So for THIS page, no n1ql:* reuse is warranted; the SDK-specific 'sdk:sqlpp-queries-with-sdk' concept correctly captures that this is fundamentally about the client library's query-issuing mechanism, which is a genuinely different kind of thing from a SQL++ statement even though it exists purely to send SQL++ text to the server. Contrast with provisioning-cluster-resources.json in this same batch, where the SDK's QueryIndexManager wraps CREATE INDEX/DROP INDEX so specifically that reuse of n1ql:create-index/n1ql:drop-index is the right call.
